slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Exod 12:5: Your lamb must be an unblemished year-old male, and you may take it from the sheep or the goats.
slides.body: “Your lamb must be an unblemished year-old male, and you may take it from the sheep or the goats.”
slides.heading: Exod 12:5

slides.alt_text: Slide 1: The claim compares an unblemished Passover animal with Christ.
slides.body: Exodus 12:5 requires an unblemished animal. Hebrews calls Christ's self-offering unblemished; 1 Peter calls his blood that of a lamb without blemish. Christians see a Passover pattern.
slides.heading: Unblemished for Passover

slides.body: The New Testament uses sacrificial purity language for Jesus. A named Christian commentary explicitly treats the Passover animal as a type of his blameless sacrifice.
slides.heading: A meaningful Christian pattern

slides.alt_text: Slide 3: The ritual does not specify a future Messiah.
slides.body: Exodus gives Israel a ritual selection rule. The animal can be from sheep or goats, and blemish rules apply to other offerings too. The analogy is coherent; the verse does not independently predict Jesus.
slides.heading: A rule, not a forecast
